claims.text: EV-TRIP-00806, EV-GPS-00806 and EV-FARE-00806 all carry trip id TRP-00806, and the trip record and the trace both fix the start of the measured segment at 2026-08-16T14:00:00+08:00, so the artifacts describe one and the same trip and the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged.

The distance that governs is the trace figure, not the trip record's rounded copy: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the measure and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. EV-GPS-00806 records 5.56 km against the 4.0 km platform optimal on EV-TRIP-00806, an excess of 1.56 km and 39.00% of optimal, which clears both establishment gates (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km). I disclose that EV-GPS-00806 is impaired: it carries weight 0.6 with issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW.

The single gap in EV-GPS-00806 — 160 seconds between 14:03:50 and 14:06:30, with a 0.83 km straight-line jump, so both a gap over 90 seconds and a jump over 500 m, impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 as well as under the pre-pass — has already been resolved the way POL-RD-07(i) requires: across an impaired stretch the excess is measured as the straight line between the bounding fixes, the reading most favourable to the driver, and the derived excess of 1.56 km is computed on a polyline that joins those bounding fixes directly. The excess is therefore the conservative figure on this trace, not an inflated one.

The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not apply. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 4.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 12.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP and tolls + 0.00 waiting fee - 0.00 promo = 10.96. Refund = 13.03 charged_total - 10.96 = 2.07, above the 0.50 de minimis, rounded up to 2.10. No separate pass-through line is added on top: erp_gantries is empty and airport_surcharge is 0.00, so there is no off-route ERP to count and POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting any of it twice.

No exculpatory clause is open on this record. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00806-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 — no advisory covers this trip window, so POL-RD-03 cannot be satisfied and any external-traffic explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13. EV-CHAT-00806 records zero messages, so no rider instruction exists that could exonerate a detour under POL-RD-04. No pickup or dropoff amendment timestamp exists and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot run, and the vehicle type is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 is irrelevant. Nothing the driver has offered displaces the arithmetic.

Nothing on the rider's side adds to the rider's burden: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 condition that would demand corroboration beyond the gps_trace — 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated — is not met. Every other field on either profile, such as the rider's prior_disputes_filed or the driver's rating and acceptance_rate, is context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not ground any finding either way.

If the judge holds that POL-RD-07(ii) bars establishing the deviation on EV-GPS-00806 alone — the chat log is empty, no ERP gantries are charged, no counterparty statement is on file, and the trip record's actual_distance_km is a copy of this same trace, so none of the independent sources the clause names exists — then POL-RD-07(iii) fixes the outcome as ESCALATE and not NO_ACTION, because the absence of proof here is a data failure rather than a finding for the driver, and POL-RD-10(3) is to the same effect. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held rather than collected, so the rider does not carry the 13.03 charge while the trace defect is resolved.

claims.text: The only artifact that measures this trip's distance, EV-GPS-00806, is impaired on its face: it is tagged IMPAIRED at weight 0.6 with issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW, because fifteen consecutive 10-second fixes are missing between 14:03:50 and 14:06:30. That is a 160-second gap between consecutive fixes inside the disputed segment, i.e. more than the 90 seconds POL-RD-07(a) permits, so the trace is impaired for policy purposes as well as for admissibility, and the polyline merely joins the bounding fixes directly rather than showing the driven road.

A deviation may not be established on an impaired trace alone. POL-RD-07(ii) requires one of four independent sources, and this bundle supplies none of them: EV-CHAT-00806 holds 0 messages, so there is no driver admission; EV-FARE-00806 carries no erp_gantries that would place the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use; dispute.counterparty_statement is null, so there is no admission of the route; and the distance figures a rider might point to — trip_record.actual_distance_km on EV-TRIP-00806 and fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km on EV-FARE-00806 — are, by their own admissibility notes, copies of this same GPS export rather than independent measurements, so neither is independent corroboration. The impaired artifact is cited here with its weight (0.6) and its issue code (GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW) disclosed.

Because the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and no corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names exists, POL-RD-07(iii) directs that the claim is not sustained on the present record and that the outcome is ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION: absence of proof across the gap is a data failure, and the disputed amount is held rather than refunded while a human reviews it. POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory. An escalated fee is not refunded, so this is the outcome that preserves the driver's position on the present record.

The excess on which the entire claim depends is carried by a single artifact, EV-GPS-00806, at weight 0.6. Under POL-GEN-02(2) a ruling's confidence must not exceed the minimum weight_multiplier among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, so confidence here is capped at 0.6, below the platform-wide 0.70 floor, and POL-RD-10(1) independently requires escalation. The 0.6 weight and the issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW are disclosed.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. Limb (b) requires an excess measured from an unimpaired gps_trace or, where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), from an independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii). This trace is impaired and no independent source exists, so no excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold is provable on this record and nothing shifts to the driver.

Even if the impaired trace were taken at face value — weight 0.6, issue GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW — the rider's own figures show a non-material deviation: a measured excess of 1.56 km / 39.00% against a 4.0 km optimal route, which clears the 20% / 0.8 km establishment gate but sits well below the 50% and 8.0 km material thresholds in POL-RD-01. This is not a MATERIAL deviation, so POL-RD-06's FULL_REFUND uplift is not available, and the rider's request to 'review the whole fare' of SGD 13.03 has no basis in the policy.

The driver's profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern and supports no adverse treatment. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 300, a ratio of 0.0, far below the 0.05 gate (with the 40-trip minimum) that POL-RD-06 sets. No pattern is established, so no balance is resolved against the driver, no FULL_REFUND uplift attaches and no driver-conduct referral arises. prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is context only under POL-GEN-01; it is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 asks for.

The one refund route that POL-RD-01 leaves open whether or not a deviation exists — a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) — yields nothing here. The fare breakdown lists no ERP gantries at all, no toll lines and an airport surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and every charged line (base 3.80, distance 3.00, time 3.36, platform fee 0.80, total 13.03) is matched by the trip record. There is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge to refund.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this case goes to a human reviewer under POL-RD-07(iii), POL-RD-10(3) and POL-RD-10(1). The disputed amount of SGD 13.03 is held — neither collected from the rider nor refunded — until that review. No money moves today.

Why. The only artifact that measures this trip's distance is the GPS trace EV-GPS-00806, and it is impaired. It is tagged IMPAIRED at weight 0.6 with issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW: fifteen consecutive 10-second fixes are missing between 14:03:50 and 14:06:30, a 160-second gap between consecutive fixes inside the disputed segment, with a straight-line jump of 0.83 km. That exceeds both the 90-second limit in POL-RD-07(a) and the 500 m limit in POL-RD-07(b), so the trace is impaired for policy purposes and not merely flagged by the pre-pass.

On an impaired trace, POL-RD-07(ii) requires an independent corroborating source before a deviation can be established. None exists here: EV-CHAT-00806 holds 0 messages, so there is no driver admission; EV-FARE-00806 charges no ERP gantries, so no gantry places the vehicle off the optimal corridor; there is no counterparty statement; and both trip_record.actual_distance_km on EV-TRIP-00806 and fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km on EV-FARE-00806 are, by their own admissibility notes, copies of this same GPS export rather than independent measurements. Under POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) the absence of proof across the gap is a data failure, not a finding for the driver, so the outcome is ESCALATE and not NO_ACTION.

Independently, POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at the weight of the artifact carrying the deciding fact — here 0.6, the weight of EV-GPS-00806 alone, since no independent carrier exists — which is below the platform floor of 0.70 and triggers POL-RD-10(1) as well.

On the rider's claims. The measured figures the rider relies on (EV-GPS-00806 trace 5.56 km against the 4.0 km optimal on EV-TRIP-00806 = 1.56 km / 39.00%) do clear the POL-RD-01 establishment gates (>20% and >0.8 km), and the rider's POL-RD-02 arithmetic is correct on its own terms: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 4.0 + 0.28 x 12.0) x 1.0 surge read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 waiting fee - 0.00 promo = 10.96, and 13.03 - 10.96 = 2.07, rounded up to 2.10. But that computation can only run once a deviation is established, and it is not, because the trace is the sole carrier of the excess and it is impaired with no independent corroboration. So no refund of 2.10 issues now. The rider's profile point is noted (deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no extra corroboration is demanded of the rider), but it does not supply the missing independent source.

On the driver's claims. The driver is right that, even taken at face value, the excess of 39.00% and 1.56 km sits below the 50% and 8.0 km MATERIAL thresholds in POL-RD-01, so no POL-RD-06 FULL_REFUND uplift would attach and no driver-conduct referral arises: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 300, well below the 0.05 ratio gate, and prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter that is context only under POL-GEN-01. The driver is also right that POL-RD-09(4) yields nothing: there is no ERP gantry line, no toll line, and a 0.00 airport surcharge on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no phantom charge to refund. Those points are accepted, but they do not change the escalation, which is driven by the impairment of the trace.

No referral fires: POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review does not apply (no pattern), POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity does not apply (no unmatched line), and POL-NS-05(ii) and POL-NS-07 are not in play.

What would resolve this on review: an independent measurement covering the 14:03:50–14:06:30 gap — an independently derived distance or route record, an ERP gantry record placing the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use, a driver or counterparty admission, or a traffic advisory covering the trip window.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute goes to a human reviewer. No money moves now, and the disputed SGD 13.03 is held rather than collected or refunded.

What the record shows. Trip TRP-00806 ran from Bishan MRT to Novena Thomson Road. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00806) stores a platform optimal route of 4.00 km / 12.0 min. The only distance measurement is the GPS trace EV-GPS-00806, which records 5.56 km — an excess of 1.56 km, or 39.00% of optimal. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km), but sits below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality thresholds.

Why we cannot rule on that excess. EV-GPS-00806 is impaired: weight 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW. Fifteen consecutive 10-second fixes are missing — a 160-second gap between 14:03:50 and 14:06:30, with a 0.83 km straight-line jump, inside the disputed stretch. That exceeds the 90-second limit in POL-RD-07(a), so the trace is impaired for policy purposes as well as under the admissibility pre-pass. Under POL-RD-07(ii) a deviation may not be established on an impaired trace alone; it needs one of four independent sources, and none exists here. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00806) holds zero messages, so there is no driver admission. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00806) charges no ERP gantries that would put the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. There is no counterparty statement. And the two other distance figures — trip_record.actual_distance_km on EV-TRIP-00806 and fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km on EV-FARE-00806 — are, by their own admissibility notes, copies of this same GPS export and not independently measured, so neither corroborates. Under POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) that is a mandatory escalation: absence of proof across the gap is a data failure, not a finding for the driver or for the rider. POL-RD-13 says the same thing where the trace itself is impaired and the missing advisory is not the deciding defect.

Independently, POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at the minimum weight of the artifact carrying the deciding fact — 0.6 here, since the excess rests solely on the impaired trace — which is below the 0.70 platform floor, so POL-RD-10(1) also requires escalation. Confidence is therefore stated at 0.6.

The arithmetic, against the day the excess is confirmed. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs (not POL-RD-11). recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 4.00 optimal km + 0.28 x 12.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge, read from EV-FARE-00806.surge_multiplier + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls - 0.00 promo = 10.96. Charged_total = 13.03, so the refund would be 13.03 - 10.96 = 2.07, rounded up to 2.10, above the 0.50 de minimis. That figure is not paid now; it is the amount available to the reviewer if the deviation is confirmed on corroborated evidence. No pass-through line is added on top: erp_gantries is empty and airport_surcharge is 0.00, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting any of it twice.

Remaining points. The driver's no-pattern point is accepted: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 300 completed trips in 90 days, below the 0.05 gate and its 40-trip minimum, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, no materiality uplift applies and no driver-conduct referral arises. The profile points raised on both sides (rating, acceptance_rate, prior_disputes_filed, prior_deviation_flags) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground nothing. No billing-integrity refund arises under POL-RD-09(4): no ERP gantries, no tolls on this trip, and no airport surcharge is charged. The bundle holds no traffic advisory covering the trip window — EV-ADVIS-00806-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and no external-traffic exoneration can be run.

What would resolve it: a GPS export that covers the gap; an independently measured trip distance (an odometer or equivalent export); ERP gantry charges placing the vehicle off the optimal corridor; a driver admission in the trip's chat log; or a counterparty statement admitting the route. The full escalation package — the reason codes, both briefs and the admissibility report — goes to the reviewer with this ruling. Both parties retain the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

ESCALATE — no money moves while this is reviewed. The SGD 13.03 fare is held rather than collected or refunded, and neither party is paid now.

Why the record cannot decide it. The distance on this trip rests on a single artifact, EV-GPS-00806, and that trace is impaired. It is tagged IMPAIRED at weight 0.6 with issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW, and it is impaired for policy purposes as well: between 14:03:50 and 14:06:30 there are no fixes for 160 seconds (POL-RD-07(a) allows at most 90), and the polyline jumps 0.83 km in a straight line across that span (over the 500 m in POL-RD-07(b)). When a trace is impaired this way, POL-RD-07(ii) says a deviation may not be established on it alone; it needs one of four independent sources, and this bundle supplies none. EV-CHAT-00806 holds 0 messages, so there is no driver admission. EV-FARE-00806 lists no ERP gantries. There is no counterparty statement. And trip_record.actual_distance_km (5.56 km on EV-TRIP-00806) and fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km (5.56 km on EV-FARE-00806) are copies of this same GPS export — their own admissibility notes say so — so neither is an independent measurement. POL-RD-07(iii) therefore directs ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, because a 160-second hole in the evidence is a data failure and not a finding for the driver, and POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory.

A second, independent reason. Even setting the impairment aside, the deciding figure — the 1.56 km / 39.00% excess, trace 5.56 km on EV-GPS-00806 against the 4.0 km optimal on EV-TRIP-00806 — is carried by one artifact at weight 0.6. Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence cannot exceed 0.6, which is below the 0.70 platform floor, so POL-RD-10(1) requires escalation on that ground too. Confidence is stated as 0.60.

The claims. The rider's claim that the deviation is established is rejected: 1.56 km over 4.0 km does clear both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%), but the impaired trace that carries it may not stand alone, and nothing independent backs it. The rider's fare claim (recomputed fare 10.96, refund 13.03 − 10.96 = 2.07, rounded up to 2.10, above the 0.50 de minimis) depends on that same deviation and falls with it — POL-RD-02 does not run. The rider's profile point is accepted: deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no extra corroboration is demanded, and every other profile field is context only under POL-GEN-01. The driver's points — that the trace is impaired, that no POL-RD-07(ii) source exists, and that confidence is capped at 0.6 — are accepted. The driver's point that this is not a MATERIAL deviation is accepted (39.00% is below the 50% and 8.0 km material thresholds), so there is no POL-RD-06 FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The driver's point that no billing-integrity refund arises is accepted: no ERP gantry, no toll, a 0.00 airport surcharge on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and every charged line (base 3.80, distance 3.00, time 3.36, platform fee 0.80, total 13.03) matches the trip record.

What would resolve it. An independent record that places the vehicle on the disputed stretch and does not derive from this trace: an ERP gantry record with coordinates the optimal route never uses, a driver admission in the chat log, a counterparty statement admitting the route, or a trip distance measured independently of this trace.
